thread:
IncidentsBot: :rotating_light: ALARM: eastus2 ALB 5xx spike detected (5m avg 18%). Alerts: ALB-targetgroup-error-rate > 10%

Devin: acked. I'm oncall. grabbing handoff from pager. standing up a quick zoom.

Devin: initial checks: ALB target health shows ~30% unhealthy behind k8s-ingress-nginx-eks-eastus2. NLB metrics look ok. Envoy stats show a surge in downstream RST and upstream 502/504 for pods handling inference routes.

Alice: seeing same in logging - tons of connection reset by peer. example from ingress logs:
```
2026-03-15T09:02:11Z ingress-proxy[envoy] upstream reset: connection_reset before response: req_id=abc123 path=/v1/generate
2026-03-15T09:02:13Z ingress-proxy[envoy] envoy outlier ejection: host ip-10-1-2-3 ejected for consecutive errors
```

Ryan: could be outlier detection aggressively ejecting healthy backends due to a brief failure window -> cascading. Outlier config was changed in last rollout (ingress v1.3.8). Deployed ~02:40 UTC.

Devin: good call. checking deploy timeline and rollout status...

Devin: `kubectl -n ingress rollout status deploy/ingress-controller` returns all pods ready, but `kubectl -n ingress get pods` shows some restart_count spikes (2-5 restarts) on 3 pods.

Maria: I can start mitigation: disable outlier detection for the ingress cluster (temporary) and set ALB deregistration delay lower to speed failover. Planning commands now.

Devin: agree. Also let's open a cross-region routing fallback to eu-west-1 for traffic from the affected AZs to avoid user impact while we stabilize. Need approvals from network.

Ryan: reconfiguring envoy config: patching ConfigMap ingress-envoy-config -> set outlier_detection: null (temporary). Patching now:
```
kubectl -n ingress patch cm ingress-envoy-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"outlier_detection":""}}'
kubectl -n ingress rollout restart deploy/ingress-controller
```

Alice: ALB target health after restart shows healthy count climbing back to 85%. CloudWatch graphs show 5xx starting to head down but still elevated.

Support-Bot: Customer impact flagged: ~12 accounts in eastus2 reporting increased latency and 502s since 09:00 UTC. Priority: P1. Ticket created IN-2319.

Devin: doing phased failover: - update route53 weight eastus2->eu-west1 (reduce weight to 10%) - add temporary header to mark rerouted traffic for tracing.

Maria: I'm executing the weight change with Network: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://failover.json` (will post change id).

IncidentsBot: Route53 change submitted: changeId /abc-route-123. propagation immediate for weighted records but TTLs still apply.

Devin: curl test to local ALB from a VM in eastus2:
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood-eastus2.example/v1/health
* Connected to api.redwood-eastus2.example (54.231.12.9) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/health HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood-eastus2.example
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< server: envoy
```
After patch and restart, same curl shows 200 for most probes but intermittent 502s.

Ryan: I dug into pod-level metrics: conntrack table on nodes hitting 90% on some worker nodes. NAT gateway ephemeral port exhaustion suspected for egress calls to model backend. Increasing conntrack and bumping NAT not ideal for long term. Will open infra ticket to increase conntrack and tune tcp_fin timeout.

Alice: adding a short-term mitigation: enable keepalive and reduce outbound concurrent connections in the ingress controller config to reduce ephemeral port churn. Patch applied.

Devin: monitoring latency and error budget. Metrics 5m avg now 6.2% down from 18%. customer calls dropping. support is sending triage messages to affected accounts.

Support-Bot: sent templated message to impacted customers, CC: account teams. Suggested wording: "We're mitigating a regional networking issue affecting eastus2. We're routing traffic to alternate region and working on ingress stability. We'll update in 30m."

Maria: handing off active pager to @Ryan for the next 30min while I join a call with network infra to confirm NAT gateway scaling. Handoff: current mitigations applied: disable outlier detection, ingress restart, Route53 weight shift, conntrack bump planned, keepalive patch applied. Monitoring links: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/ingress-eastus2 ; CloudWatch ALB: https://console.aws.../metrics

Ryan: ack. I'll keep the channel and continue to monitor. Next steps: infra to increase conntrack on nodes, optionally scale NAT gateways, and we should roll back the outlier detection removal after stabilization with a tweaked threshold. Also schedule postmortem and customer comms once stable.

Devin: agreed. I'm assigning action items: IN-2319 (customer comms), INF-449 (conntrack/NAT scale), PM-128 (postmortem + runbook update). I'll update the incident status in PagerDuty.

IncidentsBot: PagerDuty: incident 987654 acknowledged by Devin.

Alice: adding logs and example error ids to the ticket. Also capturing the ingress config diff to include in the postmortem.

Ryan: temporary mitigation holding, 5xx now down to ~2% over last 5m. Keeping watch for 30m before closing P1.

Maria: reassigning to Devin for final closure after infra confirms conntrack bump. Leaving note: don't re-enable aggressive outlier detection until we review rollout canary thresholds.

Devin: thanks team. will coordinate final close and postmortem. Creating slack incident summary now and notifying eng leadership. :thumbsup:
